targets.authors: Soto, C. J., & John, O. P.
targets.title: The next big five inventory (BFI-2): Developing and assessing a hierarchical model with 15 facets to enhance bandwidth, fidelity, and predictive power.
targets.evidence_quote:
Soto and John (2017b) investigated the psychometric
properties of the English-language BFI–2, using U.S. samples. They found evidence for the reliability, structure, and
convergent and predictive validity of the instrument. First, we wanted to examine whether the good psychometric
properties of the original BFI–2 would replicate in samples
of Dutch adults.
targets.outcome_quote:
Overall, we replicated the support
that Soto and John (2017b) reported for the structural validity of the English BFI–2, as well as the convergent validity
and internal consistency of its domain and facet scales.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall replication verdict in the conclusion takes precedence over specific psychometric discrepancies.

targets.authors: Soto, C. J., & John, O. P.
targets.title: Short and extra-short forms of the Big Five Inventory–2: The BFI-2-S and BFI-2-XS.
targets.evidence_quote:
Besides the 60-item version, Soto and John (2017a) published short (30-item) and extra-short (15-item) versions of
the BFI–2, with acceptable to good reliabilities for short Big
Five domain scales. Table 2 also displays the Cronbach’s
alphas of these shorter scales in the Dutch adaptation.
targets.outcome_quote:
The 60-item BFI–2 was
reliable at the level of both domains and facets, as were the abbreviated versions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The abbreviated forms were explicitly re-evaluated and described as reliable; weaker internal consistencies alone do not imply failure.

reasoning: New Dutch sample explicitly tests published English BFI–2 psychometric findings, including short forms. General literature on demographic correlates and validity motivated additional analyses; it is not treated as a list of individually targeted original papers. Full article identity and all five authors match.
